tools.name: get_leaderboard
tools.description:
Get the top-ranked prediction market traders (grades S, A, B only). By default in the board's own rank order; sort, dir and activity reorder and scope the same wallets as the site's leaderboard does. Supports cursor pagination and optional filters.

Args:

  - cursor (string, optional): Pagination cursor from previous response; it is bound to the sort, dir and activity it was read with
  - category (string, optional): Filter by category slug
  - strategy (string, optional): Trading style: two_sided, category_focused, high_activity, diversified, mixed, unclassified
  - sort (string, optional): rank (default), grade, volume (sports and esports USD volume), predictions, pnl, win_rate (wallets with at least 5 decided markets), edge (price_edge.edge, wallets whose edge ranks); a missing value sorts lowest
  - dir (string, optional): asc or desc; omitted, rank 1 first for rank and largest first for the rest
  - activity (string, optional): all (default), active (last trade 30 days ago or less) or inactive

Returns: Ranked list of traders with grade, score, sports and esports P&L, markets, win rate, edge over the price paid, and strategy.

tools.name: get_trader
tools.description:
Look up a prediction market trader by wallet address or username. Returns grade (S through F) and the sports and esports record: realized P&L (pnl.in_scope), markets traded, win rate, and volume. Wallet figures cover sports and esports markets only.

Optional expand fields for heavier data:
- strategy: Trading strategy classification
- categories: Per-category performance breakdown
- quant_metrics: retired since 2026-10-27; accepted and never returned, because its metrics covered every market of the wallet. Read pnl.in_scope or get_trader_pnl for the sports and esports record
- trust: Per-field provenance (source, freshness, reconciliation, completeness) for grade, P&L, and stats

A wallet address with no trader yet returns sync_status "unknown" (not an error). A username or trader id that matches no trader is a not_found error.

Args:
  - address (string, required): Ethereum wallet address (0x...) or trader username
  - expand (string[], optional): Heavy fields to include: "strategy", "categories", "trust" ("quant_metrics" is accepted and returns nothing)
  - max_age_s (integer, optional, 0 or more): Freshness ceiling in seconds. The call answers only when data_quality.status is fresh and data_quality.as_of is no older than this; otherwise it fails with reason freshness_ceiling_unsatisfied (HTTP 409). Nothing is refreshed to meet it

Returns: Trader profile with grade, P&L, stats, and optional expanded fields. The trader carries data_quality: status, as_of (the oldest clock the body rests on) and field_groups. fresh means tracked and clocked, not current: compare as_of with your own tolerance. unknown means this read cannot date that group, never that it is recent.

tools.name: get_edge_hunter
tools.description: Read the Max-only Edge Hunter API at https://0xinsider.com/sports/edge. Pro receives 403 forbidden with reason max_plan_required. One view selector offers board (default), full signals and cohort observations. All views accept kind sports|esports (omission covers both), sports, leagues, market_types, condition_ids, event_slugs, series_slugs and legacy category. Array selections accept 1..100 supplied values before deduplication, including comma-separated values inside a value; repeat REST query keys or supply MCP arrays. Lists match OR; axes match AND. Canonical sports and machine league identities normalize case-insensitively; market types and event/series slugs are exact case-sensitive provider strings. category=NFL selects the Football bucket; leagues=[nfl] selects NFL. Selection precedes the cap or pagination and appears as normalized selection beside the result fields; changed selections cannot share cursors or ETags. Every row carries nullable market_context with nullable league, series_slug, market_type and metadata_updated_at for authoritative filter discovery; metadata_updated_at is the local canonical writer clock, not provider observation time. Selected reads fail closed with 503 read_model_warming if frozen sidecar readiness is absent. Board defaults stay B grade floor, 30 rows and 48-hour horizon; min_grade S/A/B and limit clamp 1..30 are configurable, total is before the cap, with both current outcome quotes. Signals use min_grade default B, horizon default 12/clamp 1..48, limit default 20/clamp 1..100 and cursor, retaining token_id, all ranked/holder/directional/category-skill fields and clocks. Grade floor requires a holder at that grade or better without removing other holders. Observations require cohort wider_holder|in_play|emerging_pile, accept limit/cursor, and retain full observation rows, snapshot_as_of, degraded, source-generation/category funnel diagnostics and REST meta. With cohort wider_holder, admission most_held_48h opts in to the most-held selection instead: per sport, up to 8 wider_holder markets kicking off within 48 hours, most graded holders first, then volume, then soonest kickoff, at most 4 per event, recomputed every refresh and not held; every row's admitted_by is most_held_48h, the response echoes admission, and its funnel, coverage and degradation describe that selection. Required degradation_reasons names each cause with its canonical sport or null for a generation-wide cause. Degradation and coverage input_markets/capacity_limited_markets/emitted_observations/incomplete_holder_markets describe the whole all-sports generation and remain unchanged by selectors. coverage.selected_observations counts matching selected cohort rows before pagination; returned_observations counts this page. Intentional capacity_limited admission does not itself degrade a snapshot, and pagination cannot recover excluded markets. not_configured upcoming supply is not a provider failure. A selected funnel with no failure terminals does not prove the shared generation healthy. A legacy category value that cannot resolve to a sport retains its zero-work empty result: all six counts are zero and reasons are empty without reading the all-sports snapshot, so those values do not establish its health. Observation horizon stays 48h with 12h in-play kickoff lookback and 30s live snapshot ceiling; after one missed refresh, observations serve the last snapshot up to 45s longer with its age in meta.cache_age_s, and a second miss in a row returns 503; funnel accounting is not a league/type/ID selection census. All public views read warmed generations only; missing or stale readiness returns 503 read_model_warming with Retry-After 5. Advanced views use private,no-cache with REST/SDK ETag/304 helpers; board uses private,no-store and has no ETag/pagination. Invalid mode-specific parameters return 400. Price marks are market midpoints, not wallet entry prices; volume is shares. Null/db_only/degraded identify unavailable or weaker evidence. Analytics is not an order instruction.

tools.name: list_games
tools.description:
The fixture list: one coherent game per row, so an agent never has to assemble a game from market searches and team-name matching. Each row carries both sides with their provider ids and live scores, the UTC kickoff, the provider's own status, the esports series format, and the game's winner markets (the moneyline, or a soccer game's three 1X2 legs) with their condition_id, outcome token ids and provider moneyline prices. A game's spreads, totals and player props are not on the row: list_game_markets lists every market of one event_slug. Ordered by kickoff, then event_slug; games whose kickoff the provider has not published sort last. For what is on now, pass window=now: without it the list is the whole catalog and starts at the oldest game still open, which can be weeks old.

Args:
  - sport (string, optional): canonical bucket, case-insensitive, with - and _ read as a space (table-tennis and Table Tennis are one bucket). Omitted means every covered sport
  - league (string, optional): league tag as coverage.leagues spells it (nfl, epl, cs2), case-insensitive
  - status (string, optional): scheduled, live, paused, ended, postponed, cancelled, suspended, delayed, or unknown. ended, cancelled and postponed also list finished games that have left the live board (freshness.source stored) for kickoffs in starts_after..starts_before, by default the 7 days before now; such a page can be short, or empty, while has_more is true, so follow next_cursor until has_more is false
  - starts_after / starts_before (string, optional): RFC 3339 kickoff bounds; a game with no published kickoff is excluded whenever either bound is set
  - window (string, optional): all (default, the whole catalog) or now: games the provider reports in play, plus any other game whose kickoff was at most 3 hours ago or is still to come, without ended, postponed or cancelled games
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 20)
  - cursor (string, optional): opaque gms_v1_ cursor from next_cursor. It pins the page position, not a snapshot: the catalog is live, so a game added or removed between pages moves with it
  - expand (string, optional): sharp_money adds each game's sharp_money, the object get_game_sharp_money returns, read from the sport board's cached aggregate (one board read per sport, so a page stays fast). A game the board did not evaluate reads status not_computed: call get_game_sharp_money for it. A sport whose aggregate could not be read reads status unavailable while the rest of the page is served. Pro and Max

Returns: data, has_more, next_cursor, as_of, coverage and meta. tools.name: get_pick_of_the_day
tools.description:
Get the published Pick of the Day selections for today, or for a past product day with `date`, and their recorded facts. Pro opens five selections in total: the explicitly designated free selection plus the first four non-free selections in publication order. Max opens every available daily selection, up to twenty-five. Read entitled `picks` in `publication_order` order; use stable decimal-string `pick_id` for identity, not deprecated `pick_rank`. `is_free_selection` designates account access; `supersedes_pick_id` is deprecated and always null. `locked_picks` lists extra unresolved slots with only pick_rank and required_tier=max; game identity, identifying clocks and backed facts are omitted. Each full pick carries the matchup, backed side (pick_outcome_label), recorded publication price and return on the flat $1,000 stake (`stake_usd`, `return_usd`; `return_per_100` keeps the literal $100 basis), available holder facts, top grade, CLV capture status and backend-provided thesis. `scheduled_picks` contains entitled scheduled slots with release_at and kickoff; unauthorized slots appear in identity-free locked_picks instead. No market identity is revealed before publication. Withdrawn picks are omitted from current and dated recommendations, the archive and its statistics, even after market settlement. The public ledger retains every published commitment under its original identity and proof bytes.

With `date`, the tool reads that past day's slate as the dated web page shows it, under the same tier rule, with no scheduled_picks. A past day with no published pick returns not_found with param date; a past day does not change, so do not retry it. A date after today is a bad_request.

For today, when no active pick is available, the tool returns reason pick_not_released and retry_at. Schedule the next read from the returned retry guidance or an entitled scheduled slot's release_at instead of polling. An entitled published pick whose holder proof is not readable appears in `proof_pending_picks` (pick_rank, release_at, kickoff, retry_at), while `picks` contains readable picks. The tool returns read_model_warming only when no entitled published pick has readable proof. If only Max-locked selections have published, a successful state=none response carries picks=[], pick_count=0, locked_picks and an upgrade action.

For automated entry, require a present, matching, unexpired entry_authorization. Honor its returned max_entry_price and expires_at, quote a current executable book for the actual stake and retain any stricter local limits. Fees are separate; authorization guarantees neither liquidity nor execution.

Args:
  - date (string, optional): Product day (America/New_York) in YYYY-MM-DD format, on or before today; omit for today's slate

Returns: The published pick set for the current or requested product day (America/New_York); for today, a pick_not_released error with retry_at before the first pick publishes.

Every resolved outcome (win/loss/void) is public. Unentitled pending rows retain only slot/date/outcome and required_tier with backed_side_locked=true; matchup, category, league, image, publication clock and backed facts are omitted. The archive retains the included historical picks, losses included. Withdrawn recommendations are omitted from archive rows and every aggregate, including the cumulative series, even after market settlement. tools.name: get_market_wallets_in_out
tools.description:
One market's net buyers and net sellers over the last 24 hours or 7 days, live: the 0xinsider market page's wallets in/out panel for a Pro viewer. A wallet's net is its buys minus its sells in the window across both outcomes, in USD of matched notional, fees excluded.

Args:
  - condition_id (string, required): Raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id
  - window (string, optional): 24h (default) or 7d

Returns: condition_id, window, window_start and window_end (the inclusive bounds the read used), summary (wallets_in and wallets_out, the count of wallets with a positive and a negative net over every wallet in the window, and net_usd, the sum of every net), net_buyers (largest net first) and net_sellers (most negative first), at most 25 each, each wallet with its address, display_name, current grade, net_usd, trades in the window and last_traded_at (its newest trade on any market, at or before window_end), plus meta. A wallet that bought and sold the same amount nets zero and is on neither list. Reads are cached for about a minute. A condition_id with no market page answers not_found; a market outside sports and esports answers market_out_of_scope.

condition_id.description: Raw provider condition_id or the mkt_-prefixed market id

window.description: 24h (the default) or 7d, ending at the read's clock

tools.name: get_combo_fills
tools.description:
Live Polymarket combo (multi-leg) taker fills with exact decimal-string economics, wallet identity and grade, legs, conjunction result and ingest coverage. Requires a Pro or Max API key. The listing holds executions priced at most 0.95; get_combo has a combo's complete history. sort recent pages with next_cursor; largest and payout page with next_offset. A continuation can end on an empty page.

Args:
  - result (string, optional): CSV of pending, won, lost; all clears the filter
  - legs (string, optional): CSV of 2, 3, 4, 5+; all clears the filter
  - min_stake (integer, optional, default 0): Minimum collateral in whole USDC
  - min_multiplier (integer, optional, default 0): 0 disables the filter; otherwise 2 to 1000000 shares per dollar at execution
  - grades (string, optional): CSV of S, A, B, C, D, F; all clears the filter; ungraded wallets never match
  - sports (string, optional): CSV of sport slugs such as nfl, nba, soccer, esports; all clears the filter; a combo matches when any leg is in a selected sport
  - sort (string, optional): recent (default, newest first), largest (collateral), or payout (buy-fill shares, sells excluded)
  - window (string, optional): 24h, 7d or all; defaults to all for recent and 24h for largest and payout
  - limit (number, 1-200, default 50): Fills per page
  - cursor (string, optional): next_cursor from the previous recent page
  - offset (number, 0-5000, optional): next_offset from the previous largest or payout page

Returns: data (fills), has_more, next_cursor, next_offset, limit, sort, window, coverage and meta.

result.description: CSV of pending, won, lost; all clears the filter

legs.description: CSV of 2, 3, 4, 5+; all clears the filter. A combo matches any named pick count

min_multiplier.description: Minimum shares per dollar at execution: 0 (the default) disables the filter, otherwise 2 to 1000000

grades.description: CSV of S, A, B, C, D, F; all clears the filter. Ungraded wallets never match

sports.description: CSV of sport slugs such as nfl, nba, soccer, esports; all clears the filter. A combo matches when any leg is in a selected sport

sort.description: recent (the default) is newest first; largest ranks collateral; payout ranks buy-fill shares and excludes sells

window.description: Defaults to all for recent and 24h for largest and payout

cursor.description: next_cursor from the previous page; recent ordering only

offset.description: next_offset from the previous page; largest and payout ordering only

tools.name: get_combos_summary
tools.description:
The stored count of traded Polymarket combos whose YES conjunction is still pending, and when it was computed. Requires a Pro or Max API key. The count refreshes at most every five minutes and is cached for 60 seconds. A null live value is unknown, never zero.

Returns: live (count and computed_at, or null) and meta.

tools.name: get_combo
tools.description:
One Polymarket combo: legs, conjunction result, all-time trade totals, the newest 100 taker fills, lifecycle totals and ingest coverage. Requires a Pro or Max API key. Unlike get_combo_fills it keeps executions priced above 0.95. Null lifecycle or missing leg facts are unknown, never zero.

Args:
  - condition_id (string, required): Combo ID, 0x and 62 lowercase hex characters; not a binary market's condition_id

Returns: combo, fills, lifecycle, coverage, access and meta. A malformed ID is a bad_request error and an unknown one not_found.

condition_id.description: Combo ID: 0x and 62 lowercase hex characters, not a binary market's condition_id

tools.name: get_large_trade_counterparty_executions
tools.description:
Page the counterparty executions of one large trade past the first page get_large_trade embeds in counterparty_analysis. Reads the immutable snapshot that response names; a stale or changed snapshot fails with reason cursor_expired, so read get_large_trade again and restart.

Args:
  - id (string, required): Large trade ID such as wt_123 or 123
  - snapshot_id (string, required): counterparty_analysis.snapshot_id from get_large_trade
  - cursor (string, optional): executions_next_cursor from get_large_trade or from the previous page
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 100): Executions per page

Returns: executions (each with its first makers page and makers_next_cursor), executions_next_cursor, execution counts, status and meta.

id.description: Large trade ID such as wt_123 or 123

cursor.description: executions_next_cursor from get_large_trade or from the previous page

tools.name: get_large_trade_counterparty_makers
tools.description:
Page the maker wallets of one counterparty execution past the first page its execution embeds. Percentages keep the whole execution as their denominator across pages.

Args:
  - id (string, required): Large trade ID such as wt_123 or 123
  - execution_id (string, required): execution_id of the execution
  - snapshot_id (string, required): counterparty_analysis.snapshot_id from get_large_trade
  - cursor (string, optional): makers_next_cursor from the execution or next_cursor from the previous page
  - limit (number, 1-100, default 100): Makers per page

Returns: items (makers), next_cursor, execution_id, snapshot_id and meta.

id.description: Large trade ID such as wt_123 or 123

cursor.description: makers_next_cursor from the execution, or next_cursor from the previous page
